reasoning: Scheduler mutex publishes complete slot state before notifications; worker predicate remains unchanged and rechecks readiness under that mutex.

State is published under the scheduler mutex, then lock.unlock() precedes notification. Repeated notify_one calls can wake available sleepers, but need not select distinct workers if a quick callback finishes and re-waits between notifications. The unchanged readiness predicate rechecks published work under the mutex; held callbacks in this test prevent an awakened worker from consuming another job before the parallel-progress observation.
Full-pool readiness retains broadcast. No lanes, deadlines, callbacks, continuations, contexts, serialization, random state or publication ticks changed.
std::condition_variable is portable C++; no OS topology, affinity, magic thread threshold or new scheduling state.
